upright: The wielder does not age. Wounds, however, always scar.
reversed: When possible, the wielder has to attack different targets every round.

upright: The wielder's intelligence is increased by his Insight.
reversed: The wielder suffers a penalty to defend against trickery and ambushes equal to twice his Insight.

upright: The weapon is a source of Insight (up to a maximum of 5).
reversed: The wielder gains a penalty to Stealth equal to his Insight.

upright: The wielder is unnaturally beautiful; his charisma is increased by his Insight. The weapon always catches an onlooker's eye and refuses to be hidden.
reversed: The weapon almost refuses to be drawn. It may only be drawn in response to overt aggression and only as a last resort.

upright: The wielder gains a bonus to parrying equal to his Insight whenever he protects the helpless.
reversed: Fear penalties are doubled around the weapon (roughly a 100m radius).

upright: The wielder suffers -30 to using any weapon other than this one for half a year after usage.
reversed: While carrying the weapon, the wielder's unarmed attacks deal an additional D10 damage.

upright: The weapon refuses to be wielded by anyone but the summoner, leader of the binding ritual or similar person.
reversed: The weapon chooses a wielder. Once it gets fed up, it chooses a new one or specifically refuses the last one.

upright: After failing a specific attack (a simple attack, a specific maneuver, a called shot...), gain +10 to repeating the same action next round.
reversed: The wielder suffers from Fear whenever she retreats.

upright: The weapon deals additional melee damage equal to the wielder's Insight.
reversed: The weapon always needs to be braced before shooting in ranged. It cannot be used to feint in melee.

upright: The wielder only reduces his Courage by 1 for every 2 Insight.
reversed: If the wielder fights alone, he suffers -20 to all tests.

upright: The wielder may reroll one attack per session. Whenever he does, he gains 1 Corruption.
reversed: The first successful attack each session using this weapon needs to be rerolled.

upright: Anyone lying to the wielder must first pass an unmodified Courage test or swallow their words.
reversed: Whenever the weapon deals damage, the wielder takes 1 damage ignoring armor and toughness.

upright: When the wielder wishes to retreat from combat, he makes a Cr test. If he fails, he suffers D5 Corruption and does not retreat.
reversed: If the wielder is confronted with one or more sources of Fear during combat, he only tests once when combat is over and only against the strongest source.

upright: Whenever someone dies to a wound caused by this weapon, there is a chance for an otherworldly creature to enter reality. That chance is equal to the victim’s highest characteristic.
reversed: Anyone trying to move the wielder against his will suffers D5 Insight.

upright: Any attacker must succeed on a Cr test at a penalty equal to the wielder's Insight to attack him unprovoked.
reversed: All combat actions have a \emph{minimum} penalty equal to the wielder's Insight. Maneuvers with equal or higher penalties are not affected.

upright: The wielder has to fight - at least to first blood - once every week or suffer 2 Corruption every day thereafter.
reversed: When the wielder has more severe injuries than his opponent, he gains +10 to combat actions.

upright: The first hit the wielder takes every session deals double damage.
reversed: The weapon ignores all supernatural armor, and both armor and toughness of supernatural creatures.

upright: The wielder regenerates naturally every 8 hours, even without rest. He still gets tired.
reversed: The wielder may only use a single type of maneuver in each combat, e.g. only Powerstrikes.

upright: The wielder adds half of his Insight to initiative.
reversed: Everyone knows what the wielder will do next. He always counts as having the lowest initiative for the purpose of declaration.

upright: The wielder is immune to Attacks of Opportunity.
reversed: If after combat the wielder did not perform a heroic deed, nor dealt the highest damage, he needs to test against Fear and gains D5-1 Insight.

upright: The wielder can reroll one failed Restraint test against a Disabling Characteristic.
reversed: Whenever the wielder fumbles in combat, he suffers from Fear.

upright: Once per combat the wielder may take a third action during one round.
reversed: The weapon always at least requires half the user's carry weight to wield.
